findings.evidence: Draft places Table Mesh under Tagged Releases, not Top Stories, and is absent from the lede. Signed release https://primal.net/e/c5c5ad0eba413e18c10e3cd2be607e550ac818a8abaf97ccbf8fa242fbaff15f (zapstore_2026-09-24.json, SHA-256 a8f73cba1ed7b12191cb5a7544fe856611c366a632125816023f16b63b573902) is the first Android release: Bluetooth LE/Wi-Fi local tables, bundled Mensch ärgere Dich nicht and solo bots, kind 7529 + Blossom fetch with byte-hash verification. Memo INCLUDE reason is that distinctive optional Nostr module path; signed app_content says the Bluetooth mesh was tested in simulation/emulators and asks for real multi-phone reports. Draft: “tested in simulation and emulators, not yet at real multi-phone tables” and “Nostr is used to discover and deliver optional games; the actual table session runs locally without an internet connection or account.”
findings.recommendation: Retain Tagged Releases INCLUDE; do not elevate to Top Stories. The optional kind-7529/Blossom/hash path is a real first-release Nostr surface, but emulator-only mesh testing and non-core Nostr usage would make Top Story placement unjustified.
findings.title: Table Mesh 0.1.0 INCLUDE is 8/10 at Tagged Releases, not a Top Story

findings.evidence: Draft Table Mesh: “Nostr is used to discover and deliver optional games; the actual table session runs locally without an internet connection or account.” Signed release notes at https://primal.net/e/c5c5ad0eba413e18c10e3cd2be607e550ac818a8abaf97ccbf8fa242fbaff15f: “Find more games on Nostr (kind 7529), downloaded from Blossom and verified byte for byte” / “searches Nostr for game releases (kind 7529) and downloads them from Blossom.” The draft does not say Nostr carries table moves.
findings.recommendation: Tighten to “Nostr is used to discover optional games, which are fetched from Blossom and hash-checked; the table session itself runs locally and does not carry moves over Nostr.”
findings.title: Second-paragraph “deliver” slightly compresses Blossom fetch onto Nostr

summary: On this immutable snapshot only, the two final-cutoff story decisions and their wording hold: MDK #2007 is described as merged library work after the 0.10.4 tag, matching the captured PR-body facts and inventing neither measured latency nor deployed client behavior; Table Mesh 0.1.0 is a first signed Android release whose Bluetooth/Wi-Fi local play, bundled Mensch ärgere Dich nicht and bots, kind-7529 discovery, and Blossom byte verification are supported by the signed-store artifact, without implying that Nostr carries table moves or that real multi-phone testing is complete.
